change: Not admitted. The scored judge is always gated by a downstream exact evaluation, and no judge false-accept or exploitation rate is measured, so it gives no k* or q for G2/T2. Its judge is stronger than the worker, so it does not bear on G4 either. It is a useful compute-accounting example for C2 (CPU hours, wall clock and API cost are reported separately, including judge calls).
summary: SIFT prefilters candidate self-modifications with pairwise LLM-judge comparisons (regularized Bradley-Terry) and runs full benchmark evaluation only on top nodes; on Polyglot-225 with a Qwen3-30B coder it reports 31.1% vs HGM 30.5%, DGM 27.1%, SICA 25.1% (224 vs 347 CPU hours for HGM, single run), and 35.1% with o3-mini (repeats 35.1/32.0/35.6%). Judge rank vs true score Spearman rho was +0.40 (diffs only) to +0.68 (full files) on Polyglot; the authors note the judge is stronger than the coding backbone.
title: Self Improvement via Fast Tree-search (SIFT)

change: Not admitted: this is harness efficiency found by a fixed search loop. It has no second-order, transplant or evaluator-exploitation measurement, so it leaves T0 unchanged (and supports it as ordinary search plus selection).
summary: Auto-research loops at the harness layer selected four mechanisms (action execution, context compaction, observation handling, delegated reading). On the 51-task EdgeBench the result matches the Pi harness across GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 while cutting recorded token traffic by 44.7-49.0% and API cost by about one third (abstract only read).
title: SoL-Pi: Recursively Scaling Auto-Research Loops for Efficient Agent Harness

change: Not admitted: submitted 2026-09-01, outside this pass's window, and it evolves worker harnesses, not the improver. Worth a later pass as real-system evidence for B6's 'feedback up / held-out down' shape and as a caution for H1/T8 (substrate portability is conditional).
summary: Six creator LLMs build and then evolve agent harnesses across four domains (2,207 downstream instances). Evolution gains on visible feedback shrink on held-out tasks (Qwen 3.7 Max +13.9 to +1.43; DeepSeek V4 Pro +13.4 to +3.17), and harness capability ports across executor models only when compatible (an Opus-built harness fell from 69.3 to 33.0 on SWE-bench Pro under a Gemini executor). An audit found no harness scoring through a prohibited route; the same commit varies by about +/-4.75 pair-score points.
title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?

change: Not admitted: it measures the degree of AI involvement in first-order R&D tasks (a capability/automation index), not second-order improvement of an improver, so L2's answer (only Hyperagents imp@k, HGM metaproductivity, AIDE^2) is unchanged; no transplant, compute-matched or evaluator-exploitation data.
summary: Anthropic (Marina Favaro, Phillie Wright) reports that as of August 2026 Claude 'leads' (Epoch AI scale AL4) 26% of its AI R&D work, up from under 1% in February 2026, that over 90% is at AL3 or above, and that 0% is at AL5 (fully autonomous); online monitors blocked 0.002% of actions with about 30,000 agents deployed. The page itself is dated August 2026 in the fetch; the public disclosure was reported by Bloomberg and others on 2026-09-17, and the authors note Claude helped build the task inventory and scores (correlated-judge risk).
title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs (Anthropic R&D Automation Index)

change: Not admitted: outside the window (v2 2026-09-09) and the abstract reports no transplant, memory-strip or compute-matched evidence, so nothing in T0, B1 or O1 changes; a future pass could read the body for a meta-policy transfer arm.
summary: A 31-author paper (first author Zihan Tan; v1 2026-09-06, v2 2026-09-09) composes three typed operators (Data-RSI, Harness-RSI, Model-RSI) under a two-axis optimizer that chooses operator order and proposal policy, with a meta-level policy revising the schedule. Only the abstract page was read; it gives no numbers on transfer of the meta-level policy, compute matching or seeds.
title: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves

change: Not admitted: relevant in kind to T6 (out-of-support probes) and D6, but only the abstract was read and no numbers were obtained to say whether out-of-distribution counterfactual probes reduced false admissions; worth a full-text read next pass.
summary: Zhu, Huang, Yin, Xie, Zhang and Zhou propose CHASE, in which a Challenger searches, after each harness update, for semantics-preserving protocol transformations that destroy the claimed gain, building a finite counterfactual archive linked in theory to an ideal shortcut-neutralised benchmark. Evaluated on Syn-Ledger and OfficeQA; v3 2026-09-24; abstract only read, numbers unknown.
title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts (CHASE)

change: Not admitted: measures per-agent adoption after injection, not onward transmission, so no R0 or threshold is estimated and T5/F1 are not changed.
summary: Wu, Ying, Wu, Zheng, Cheng, Shi and Guo frame multi-agent loss of control as mutation, contagion and recovery and test it on RogueHandoff-20 (20 executable scenarios) with a modified Qwen-27B route. Harm rates rose from 0-5% on normal tasks to 40-95% after unsafe-trajectory injection, 5-45 points above direct malicious requests, and the authors state they do not establish natural rare-event rates or an autonomous cascade.
title: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery

change: Not admitted because it is two months outside the window, but flagged to the seat: offspring = degree x constant adoption (2 x 0.333, 5 x 0.333) crossing 1 is a real-model reading of T5's R0 = d tau (1 - v) being linear in d, from one model on 36 tasks.
summary: Niu, Shu and Zhao build a correction-aware SEICS network model and test it with 21,000 simulated trajectories and grok-4.3 on 36 tasks. Raising node degree from 2 to 5 took first-generation error offspring from 0.667 to 1.667 while adoption among exposed neighbours stayed at 0.333 (abstract read).
title: Reliability-Contagion Feasibility in LLM Multi-Agent Networks
